provider: SURF Research Drive (Netherlands) — up to 5 TB free via NWO-funded Small Compute applications

free_tier.stated: You will receive up to 5 TB of storage space.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: The Research Drive page describes storing, sharing and synchronising research data and gives no per-object size or count cap.

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: The Research Drive page describes storing, sharing and synchronising research data and gives no retention period.

egress.terms: Unmetered. SURF is the Dutch national e-infrastructure, no egress product exists.

tooling: Research Drive is ownCloud/Nextcloud-based, so the standard desktop sync client and WebDAV endpoints work; rclone's webdav backend applies. Not S3.
chaining: A Small Compute application for Data Processing on Grid and/or Spider can include up to 200TB disk storage, 300TB tape storage, Research Drive - via SURF (up to 5TB) or via institution
limits_note: Per-object-cap: not published for Research Drive; the SURF bundle page caps 'max. 10TB project space storage' on Snellius and 'up to 200TB disk storage' on Grid/Spider. request-rate: not published. Retention: tied to the project; SURF states data is retained for the project duration. Gate: 'researchers must have either a tenured appointment .. or a tenure track appointment at one of the research organisations listed'. A genuinely institution-gated, NWO-funded scheme.

You will receive up to 5 TB of storage space.' Institutional instances have their own (much larger) quotas set per institution.
extras.limits_verbatim: per-object-cap: not published for Research Drive; the SURF bundle page caps 'max. 10TB project space storage' on Snellius and 'up to 200TB disk storage' on Grid/Spider. request-rate: not published. Retention: tied to the project; SURF states data is retained for the project duration. Gate: 'researchers must have either a tenured appointment ... or a tenure track appointment at one of the research organisations listed' — a genuinely institution-gated, NWO-funded scheme.
extras.egress_verbatim: Unmetered — SURF is the Dutch national e-infrastructure, no egress product exists.
extras.chaining_verbatim: 5 TB per project via Small Compute, and the same application also unlocks 'max. 10TB project space storage' on Snellius, 'up to 200TB disk storage, 300TB tape storage' on Grid/Spider for data processing, and 'max. 50TB offline tape storage' — one NWO-funded application can therefore land 200+ TB of storage plus 5 TB of Research Drive. That is the single best storage-per-application ratio I found.
extras.tooling_verbatim: Research Drive is ownCloud/Nextcloud-based, so the standard desktop sync client and WebDAV endpoints work; rclone's webdav backend applies. Not S3.
extras.agent_focus: National and regional research-data infrastructure that hands out free (or grant-funded) bulk object storage to researchers: EUDAT/B2SHARE, EOSC EU Node, SURF, GÉANT ecosystem, NIRD/Sigma2, CSC Allas + LUMI-O, NAISS, DeiC, EuroHPC, DARIAH/CLARIN/ELIXIR nodes, NCI, ARDC Nectar, Digital Alliance of Canada, ACCESS/OSN, TACC, NCAR, NRP. Central question: which of these are SELF-SERVICE (anyone can get a login and a bucket) versus INSTITUTION-GATED (you need a university appointment, a national research affiliation, or a reviewed proposal). The per-project quotas here are the largest numbers in the whole survey — 10-150 TB — so the gate, not the quota, is the finding.
